fields.meta_description: Build a 360 survey with confidential rater groups and a self-versus-others report for each person. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a 360 Survey Your Managers Can Act On
fields.hero_description: Describe who gets reviewed and who rates them. Emergent builds the nomination flow and a confidential report for each person, on a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a 360 Survey Needs to Work
fields.features_subheading: A 360 survey rates one person through the eyes of their manager, peers and direct reports, next to their own self-rating.
fields.feature_1:
Rater groups you define

Sorts every rater into a group: manager, peers, direct reports, or customers if you want an outside view. Each group gets its own score, and the self-rating sits beside every one.
fields.feature_2:
Nominations with a manager check

Lets each participant nominate their own raters, then sends that list to their manager to approve or edit. Invites go out only after approval, each one carrying a personal link.
fields.feature_3:
Group minimums that protect raters

Folds any rater group below your minimum, such as three, into an Others line on the report. The manager's rating is the exception and keeps its own label, and raters know it.
fields.feature_4:
Self against others on every item

Plots the self-rating against everyone else's average for each item and ranks the gaps. The widest ones sit at the top of the report, which is where a coach starts the debrief.
fields.feature_5:
Comments stripped of names

Collects open comments under each competency and removes rater names first. Comments from a group under the minimum move to the Others section along with that group's scores.
fields.feature_6:
The whole 360 app in GitHub

Exports the full app to your GitHub on paid plans, from the nomination flow to the rating database. Run next year's cycle from your own code, or keep changing it in Emergent.

fields.tab_content_1:
Dana scores herself a 4.5 on delegating

Each of the 14 new managers in Northwind's leadership program gets a report on 10 items, with the self-rating beside the average of everyone else. Dana Reyes rated herself 4.5 on delegating work. Her nine raters averaged 3.1. That 1.4 gap is the widest on her report and the first topic in her coaching session.
fields.tab_content_2:
Peers nominated on Monday, reminded by Thursday

Participants pick six peers on Monday, and their manager approves or edits the list before anything is sent. Each approved rater gets an email with a personal link. Anyone who has not answered after three days gets one reminder on Thursday, and the window closes on day 10.
fields.tab_content_3:
Two direct reports, folded into Others

Two direct reports answered Marcus Lee's survey, one short of the minimum of three. Their ratings join one customer rating in an Others line of three instead of showing on their own. His manager's single rating keeps its own label, and his five peers clear the minimum as a group.
fields.tab_content_4:
The same raters, six months on

Six months after the first round, each manager picks the three items they worked on, and the same raters score only those. Dana's delegation score rose from 3.1 to 3.8. Her report shows both rounds side by side, pulled from the same table that holds round one.

fields.howto_description: A 360 earns the trust of its raters in the first round or loses it. Settle the purpose and the confidentiality rules before any invite goes out.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write items a rater can observe
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Set rater groups and a minimum
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose whether the report stays with the person and their coach or also reaches HR for pay and promotion. HR practitioners warn that 360 feedback is often misused as performance management. Put the answer in the first invite, and keep it for every round that follows.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Rate behaviors, not traits. "Gives clear deadlines when handing off work" can be scored by a peer, while "is a strong leader" cannot. Keep the set between 10 and 15 items on a 1-5 scale, with two open comment boxes at the end.
fields.howto_step_3_des: List the groups each person will hear from: manager, peers, direct reports and any outside raters. Then set the smallest group that may show on its own, commonly three. Ask for enough nominations that each group can clear it.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write out the participants, the items, the rater groups, the minimum and the dates in plain English. Emergent builds the whole round, with each rating stored as a row in a table you own. Changing an item later takes one more message.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Tell raters how their answers travel
fields.howto_step_5_des: Before invites go out, tell raters who reads the report and that small groups merge into Others. Name the one exception, the manager's rating, up front. Raters should hear this before they start, not after the report opens.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Hand the report over in person
fields.howto_step_6_des: Nobody should open a 360 report alone for the first time. A coach or HR partner walks through the widest self-versus-others gaps and the comments behind them. The person leaves with two or three behaviors to work on, written down.
fields.howto_step_7_des: About six months later, send the same raters only the items each person chose to work on. A short second round shows whether the change was visible to others, and it costs raters a few minutes instead of a full survey.

plan.angle: The top 10 is glossary definitions (Agendrix, BambooHR, Allvoices), long guides (Questback, CustomInsight) and platform pages (Qualtrics, LimeSurvey, g360), plus a SurveyMonkey question list. None shows the mechanics that decide whether a 360 is trusted: who nominates raters, how small rater groups stay confidential, where self-ratings and others' ratings split, and a second round that shows whether coaching moved anything. This page defines the term up top for the AI Overview, answers the PAA questions on cost, tools, free options and examples, and shows a leadership 360 a company owns as an app.
